what: Copies of OAIY's leaf-script contract, vendored so FormLogic can hold the profile it serves
to OAIY's own rules without depending on a sibling checkout. formlogic.com and oaiy.com are
separate repositories with separate release trains: an import across them would make a
FormLogic test pass or fail on whichever revision of oaiy.com happens to be on the disk, and
would make FormLogic unbuildable for anyone who does not have that checkout at all.
The failure this guards against is the one that already happened once: the plans this work
came from described a profile body of {v, id, revision, preamble, preambleSha256,
instructionSteps, budgetsMs, hooks} with a python section carrying kinds and lineOffsets.
OAIY's schema is additionalProperties:false at the top level AND inside `python`, so every
one of those extra keys is a refusal, not an ignored field. Validating the served document
against this copy is what turns that from a discovery at integration time into a red test.
The schema now carries `python.modes`: the wrappings a job may name, each with the files it
adds, the block file, the text before and after the author's source, and the generated line
count a runner subtracts from whatever line the engine blames. FormLogic serves all five of
its own, so a consumer holding only the profile can build the project and answer in the
author's line numbers. The strictness cuts the other way too: a host on the older schema
refuses a profile carrying modes, which is correct - it would otherwise build a project with
no entry module at all.
REFRESHING: re-copy the schema verbatim (no reformatting - scriptProfile.test.ts recomputes
the git blob hash and compares it to schema.blobSha1, so a copy that differs by a byte fails),
re-read the three name lists from the paths below, and update every commit and blob here.

vendoredFrom.repo: oaiy.com (sibling checkout; formlogic.com does not depend on it)
vendoredFrom.note: Taken at the commit that widened the schema with `python.modes` ("A profile can describe how to wrap a leaf script..."). The previous copy was read at 224cb83; the schema changed in this commit, and `scriptEnvelopeGlobals` grew by three names in aeadafe (the commit between them), which is why the lists below are re-read and not only the schema.

schema.lastChangedSubject: A profile can describe how to wrap a leaf script, and the runner does the wrapping — including subtracting its own lines from whatever line the engine blames

what: Names a served preamble may not DECLARE at any level a text scan can see. OAIY refuses such
a profile twice over: `detectPreambleCollision` (zipp-script.ts) is a text scan the browser
envelope runs, and `parseScriptProfile` (cli/src/zipp/profile.ts) re-checks it against the
syntax tree with a wider list. build-script-profile.mjs applies the UNION, because a profile
has to be acceptable to both consumers and the generator is the only place that can refuse
before the document is committed.
The scan is deliberately indent-tolerant on OAIY's side (its regex leads with whitespace), so
a `var host = ...` nested three functions deep inside prelude.js is a refusal even though it
shadows nothing at the top level. FormLogic's prelude declares 74 names under that scan
(12 of them at the top level) and none of them is on this list - but `db`, `host` and
`window` are ordinary local-variable names, so this is a live hazard, not a theoretical one.
The `var`s OAIY's guest shims declare at program top level, emitted immediately before the
profile preamble (`buildScriptProgram`, zipp-script.ts). A preamble that redeclares one of
these with let/const/class is a SyntaxError that takes the whole program, and the CLI refuses
it (`parseScriptProfile`'s second loop). A `var` or `function` of the same name is legal and
REPLACES the stub, which OAIY allows as a deliberate choice - so only lexical declarations
are checked against this list.
